**7 findings across 4 blocker, 2 major, 1 minor severity:**

| # | Severity | Rule | Line | Issue |
|---|----------|------|------|-------|
| 1 | BLOCKER | make_illegal_states_unrepresentable | 1 | `status: String` + `bool` flags allow impossible state combinations |
| 2 | BLOCKER | type_newtypes_for_domain_primitives | 2 | `id: String` accepts any value including empty/invalid |
| 3 | BLOCKER | no_bool_lifecycle_flags | 4 | Independent `is_validated`/`is_sent` booleans break transition ordering |
| 4 | MAJOR | functional_core_imperative_shell | 9 | `mark_sent` mutates in-place with no precondition checks |
| 5 | MAJOR | allocation_without_try_reserve | 10 | Unnecessary `String::to_string()` allocation per call |
| 6 | MINOR | missing_benchmark_evidence | 1 | No benchmarks for performance-relevant paths |
| 7 | MINOR | missing_command_evidence | 1 | No tests, clippy, or fmt evidence |

**Root cause**: The entire crate violates the Power-of-Ten principle — the typestate is representable as flat booleans and a free-form string, making illegal states constructible and unverifiable at compile time. The fix is a single `LedgerStatus` enum with typed variants replacing all three flat fields.
